parameters.content:
## Reusable platform service: Agent Governance

**Input** `requesting_workflow`, `proposed_action`, `action_type` (read | write | send | delete | pay | deploy | ...), `affected_system`, `parameters` (JSON string), `agent_reasoning`, `agent_confidence`, `idempotency_key`, `override_token`, `simulate_decision`.

**Output** `{ decision, approved, risk_level, risk_reasons[], decided_by, decision_reason, requested_at, decided_at, expires_at, latency_ms }`

## Risk policy

| Level | Route |
| --- | --- |
| LOW | execute immediately |
| MEDIUM | five deterministic policy checks, then execute or escalate |
| HIGH | human approval |
| CRITICAL | **denied by default**; a valid `override_token` only buys a human review, never an approval |

An unrecognised `action_type` defaults to **HIGH**, never LOW. Levels can only ever be raised. A request whose text argues that it is pre-approved or does not need approval is treated as a suspected prompt injection and raised to CRITICAL.

## Fail closed

The Telegram approval waits 60 minutes. A timeout, a channel error or a malformed response all resolve to **rejected** — never to approved. Simulated decisions used by the test harness are written to the ledger with `decided_by = "simulated:test-harness"` so they can never be mistaken for a real human approval during an audit.
